title: Sima Chengzhen
subtitle: 647–735 · Tang Daoist figure
evidence: Historically documented · traditional layers also present
shortSummary: Sima Chengzhen connects mountain cultivation, textual traditions and Tang court networks.
curatorialDescription: Sima Chengzhen matters not only as an individual biography but as a figure crossing three spaces: mountains, lineage and court. Tang Daoism could appear as mountain cultivation while also entering imperial ritual and patronage.
A relation graph must distinguish lineage tradition, documented activity and later veneration. They may concern one figure but belong to different evidence layers.
His case also shows why Daoist philosophical concepts and organised Daoism are not identical, even when textual interpretation and practice connect them.
researchNote: The first release shows only foundational relations among court, mountain cultivation and textual tradition. Lineage detail will expand after source and tradition review.
